claims.text: Introducing a hierarchical microstructure with nanoscale precipitates and engineered grain boundaries will improve the combination of strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance relative to conventional single-phase HEAs.
Thermomechanical processing can induce nanoscale precipitate formation in the HEA.
Thermomechanical processing can refine or otherwise optimize the HEA's grain-boundary structure.
Controlling processing temperature and strain rate can prevent excessive grain growth and precipitate coarsening.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by nanoscale precipitates increases strength.
Refined grain boundaries enhance ductility by promoting grain-boundary sliding.
Refined grain boundaries enhance fracture resistance by promoting crack deflection.
The hierarchical microstructure balances precipitation strengthening and grain-boundary-mediated deformation or toughening to optimize mechanical properties.
The processed HEA will exhibit more than a 20% increase in strength relative to the same HEA in its homogeneous single-phase state.
The processed HEA will exhibit more than a 10% increase in elongation to failure relative to the baseline.
The processed HEA will exhibit more than a 15% increase in fracture toughness relative to the baseline.
The processing will cause only a minimal change in Young’s modulus.
The proposed improvements may not occur when the alloy composition is not conducive to precipitate formation.
The proposed improvements may not occur when processing causes excessive grain growth or precipitate coarsening.
